newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP dip draws Australia stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP dip draws Australia stocks to lower close.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2359 -3 US 30yr cl 6.79 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.375 -0.090 Gold (NY cl) $380.60
*Shares end lower, weighed down by a weak showing from bellwether issue BHP. Volume 328.7 million shares, value A$804.8 million, 1,003 stocks traded, 323 steady, 345 rises, 335 falls

Australian shares ended lower on Tuesday with selling of major resource issues BHP and CRA the main source of weakness after base metal prices continued to soften on the London Metal Exchange on Monday.

The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 8.1 points lower at 2,331.7, but off its intra-day low of 2,326.3. The December share price index closed three points down at 2,359 and at a 27.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said turnover was boosted by the debut of life office National Mutual but otherwise trading was featureless with little news to interest investors in the market.
"The weak resource sector and the National Mutual listing were the main features of the market," said Tony Russell, a dealer at Brisbane firm, Morgan Stockbroking.

Russell said despite today's fall he expected investor sentiment would remain mostly positive for the Australian market in the near term as it mirrored Wall Street in the lead up to the U.S. presidential election.
Dealers said National Mutual shares debuted at a healthy premium as had been expected after the life office's share offer was heavily oversubscribed by institutional investors in September.
Resource major WMC was one of the most active issues on the day after the company said it would implement cost cut measures at its Kambalda nickel/gold mine in Asia.
Among the weaker industrial issues on the day were Commonwealth Bank and paper manufacturer Amcor.

Commonwealth Bank stock slipped following comments from the chairman at the bank's annual meeting in Melbourne while dealers judged that Amcor's fall was tied to continued investor concern about the outlook for international paper prices.
In other markets Australian bonds were weak from the opening with a government bond adding to the softer tone ahead of local employment data to be released later this week.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds finished at 7.61 percent, 0.09 percent above Monday's close.
The Australian dollar inched lower in choppy trade. At 5.20 p.m. (0720 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7879/84.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was busier with futures trading lifted by the the return of Sydney traders after a public holiday. Total options traded 40,509 (39,224).
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 6,969 (1,383).
